summary:
National Capital Region stands under the national framework of the Philippines. Within Metro Manila, Quezon City has enacted a municipal ordinance, sponsored by Councilors Bernard Herrera and colleagues, requiring all city public health facilities to provide gender-affirming consultations and counselling, mental-health support, and medical guidance and referrals regardless of a patient's gender identity or expression. Mayor Joy Belmonte stated the measure removes longstanding healthcare barriers for gender-diverse and transgender residents.

Trans-specific violence has occurred inside the region. Shaina Bayabay, a 29-year-old trans woman in Pasig City, was killed on 1 March 2024; the memorial record categorises the case as violence and the cause as strangulation, and the underlying report states she was killed during a drinking session.
tangentialFactors: The Quezon City ordinance is a municipal-level protection that operates alongside, and does not replace, the absence of a national SOGI anti-discrimination statute and the patchwork of local ordinances elsewhere in the country.
localsOnly: Quezon City's ordinance binds city-run public health facilities, so residents and patients there can invoke it when seeking gender-affirming consultations, counselling, mental-health support and referrals. It does not govern privately operated clinics outside the city system.
outOfScopeNotes: The source inventory does not resolve whether the Quezon City ordinance carries an enforcement mechanism, penalties for non-compliance, or funding commitments, nor whether other cities in National Capital Region have comparable health-facility mandates. The circumstances of Shaina Bayabay's killing, including any arrest, charge or conviction, are not sourced here.
